newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Yen, mark rally in low Hungary FX futures trade.
newsitem.headline: Yen, mark rally in low Hungary FX futures trade.

text.p: Hungary's currency futures volume on Monday was low, with the Budapest Commodities Exchange (BCE) recording 2.3 billion forints ($13.3 million) in turnover and the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) registering no trades.

Despite the sluggish activity, the yen managed to grab some interest with 6,795 contracts traded, half of the total 11,541 lots traded. September and December contracts rose by 1.1 forints and 72 fillers, respectively, to 158.30 and 163.72 forints per 100 yen.
"The yen's popularity and its rise reflect recent rises against the dollar on the spot market," said Swap's Janos Szolyka.
But some dealers said they preferred to stay on the sidelines amid the current turbulence in dollar/mark and dollar/yen rates.
"The yen is too risky at the moment," said Gyorgy Adamosi of PTT Brokers. "We prefer quieter currencies like the Swiss franc."
The mark also rose between 10 and 40 fillers for March, September and December to 105.00, 113.40 and 117.15 forints, respectively.
All dollar contracts eased between 88 fillers and 1.5 forints, with December falling the most from 194.30 to 192.80 forints.
BSE dealers said the dollar's recent fall coupled with healthy interest on Monday in BCE futures may have contributed to the lack of currency futures trade there.
"It's such a small market that it's much easier to say why something happens than why nothing happens," said Robert Cselovszki of WestLB Investment.
-- Duncan Shiels, Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040 ($ = 173.5 Hungarian Forints)
